explanation: A walk by a lake in April 1802 inspired it. His sister Dorothy described the same daffodils in her journal, which he drew on.

claims.text: In I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud, the poet sees a host of golden daffodils.
The flowers in the poem are not roses, bluebells or tulips.
The poem grew from a walk Wordsworth took with his sister Dorothy beside Ullswater in April 1802.
Dorothy Wordsworth described the same daffodils in her journal, which the poem drew on.
